tasks.subject: Implement canonical live setup and trigger preview (quality gate)
tasks.description: Implement the approved canonical two-stage engine using Web semantics as reference, with immutable contracts, closed-daily setup detection, current-session persisted-data adapter, intraday trigger evaluation, stable IDs, multiple setups, ORCL fixtures/tests, focused MCP preview tool on the existing service, and documentation. Do not migrate Web production routing or legacy scanner. Do not call broker/order/Telegram/scheduler/LLM surfaces.
tasks.objective: Add a deterministic read-only canonical live preview engine for LONG LP1/LP2/PRB1/PRB2 with setup/entry-day separation and MCP exposure, while leaving legacy Web and scanner paths untouched.
acceptance: Historical setup detection uses only closed daily bars and never includes the current session row.
CurrentSessionState explicitly includes session date, OHLCV, as-of, completeness, source, timeframe, persisted intraday timestamp, and freshness.
LONG LP1, LP2, PRB1, and PRB2 each have split historical setup and entry-day trigger semantics matching the Web reference.
WATCH, READY, REJECTED, STALE_DATA, INVALID, and NO_SETUP are deterministic; stale data cannot be READY.
Multiple setups per symbol are preserved with deterministic stable setup IDs across WATCH to READY.
ORCL Setup A and B produce WATCH; synthetic Setup B high above entry produces READY with unchanged setup ID.
A focused preview MCP tool is added to the existing service without changing run_universe_scan or adding a service/port.
No broker, order, scheduler, Telegram, LLM, Web production, or legacy scanner migration is introduced.
Documentation covers contracts, statuses, provenance, and READY is not approval.
